lean.statement:
{E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (μ : Measure E) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {η : ℝ} (hη : 0 < η) :
    let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
      (fun p : E × E => (p.1, p.1 + Real.sqrt η • p.2))
    let ν := J.snd
    ∃ D : Lp ℝ 2 ν →ₗ.[ℝ] Lp E 2 ν,
      Dense (D.domain : Set (Lp ℝ 2 ν)) ∧ D.IsClosable ∧ D.closure.IsClosed ∧
      ∀ (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) (v : Lp E 2 ν), (u,v) ∈ D.graph ↔
        ∃ f : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ f ∧ HasCompactSupport f ∧
          u =ᵐ[ν] f ∧ v =ᵐ[ν] gradient f
approved_definition_context: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its norm and Borel measurable structure, including rank zero. μ is any actual probability measure and η is any positive real number. No finite-moment, density, potential or gradient-domain hypothesis is supplied.

stdGaussian E is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. J is the displayed measurable pushforward of the independent product of μ and this Gaussian, with second coordinate x+sqrt(η)g. ν=J.snd is its actual second marginal.

Lp ℝ 2 ν and Lp E 2 ν are the actual spaces of square-integrable almost-everywhere classes under ν, with real scalar and E-valued representatives respectively. AE equalities in the conclusion use this same actual ν.

LinearPMap is a genuine real linear operator with a linear-subspace domain, not an everywhere-defined formal function. D.graph is its actual set of domain/value pairs. Dense domain means norm-topological density in scalar L2. IsClosable means its graph closure is single-valued; D.closure is that operator closure and IsClosed means its actual graph is closed.

One D is produced for the fixed μ and η before all u and v. For every actual scalar/vector L2 pair, graph membership is equivalent to existence of a globally smooth compactly supported real f with u represented by f and v represented by its genuine real gradient. The gradient is inverse Riesz of the actual Frechet derivative.

The conclusion provides dense domain, closability and closed closure, with the exact smooth-compact graph. It makes no claim that an arbitrary conditional integral is in the closure domain or that a rough-input energy/mixing/query-cost bound is proved.
